candidates.severity: unassigned; conditional divergence between the global wedding selector and its canonical-world settlement policy
candidates.classification: New bounded 95e scheduling-authority assessment linked to an earlier open lifecycle queue question; not an observed delayed ceremony.
candidates.first_failed_contract: The private recurring NPC tick calls the combined global lifecycle queue before selecting its bounded NPC cohort. A due wedding is retained by that queue only if a participant has a recorded death at or before the ceremony or both participant personal clocks have reached the effective minute. The wedding settlement owner instead ignores its participant-frontier argument and selects by refreshed official world time; its stated policy says subjective clocks do not delay ceremonies. An ordinary personal-clock lifecycle write also calls that owner directly without the global processability gate. Therefore the same due, living engagement is selected or skipped based on which caller reaches it.
candidates.conditional_example: Assume the official time has reached a valid reserved wedding, no participant has a recorded death at or before the ceremony, at least one existing personal clock is earlier than the ceremony, and neither participant receives a separate lifecycle time write during the scheduler tick. Even with available global queue capacity, the combined queue filters out the wedding before dispatch. A direct personal-clock settlement after the same official time would invoke the due-wedding owner, subject to its separate alive, age, residence and other checks. The bounded NPC cohort can later advance a participant and trigger the direct path; no indefinite delay, observed actual schedule, or guaranteed completed marriage is claimed.
candidates.scope_and_safeguards: The source filters not-ready entries before the queue capacity limit, so this finding does not assert they starve other events. The dead-participant branch is deliberately processable for cancellation. Birth and secret-discovery frontiers have distinct policies and must not be generalized from weddings. An unrelated earlier finding concerns caught post-write wedding errors; the prior capacity-specific assessment remains separate.
candidates.connected_repair: After the audit gate decide one authoritative wedding chronology and apply it consistently across global scheduling, direct lifecycle settlement, due/death checks and effective-date projections, without advancing a player clock merely to manufacture readiness. Preserve deterministic queue ordering and bounds, historical occupancy and active-commitment semantics, dead-participant cancellation, and separate birth/discovery frontiers. Reconcile existing wedding failure and capacity obligations independently.
candidates.later_acceptance: After separately authorized work, examine official time at and around the ceremony with participants behind, equal and ahead; independent scheduler tick versus participant clock writes; absent/dead participants; bounded capacity and birth ordering; and historical observer projections. None ran.
candidates.discovery: partial; intended policy, full scheduling callers and reachable real actor states, lifecycle ordering and historical aliases remain open

remaining: Resolve canonical-world versus subjective-frontier wedding policy, trace every caller and actual scheduling reachability, reconcile the full historical queue and independent lenses. Original final 3821 ledger and queue remain missing.
